Cauchy-Schwarz inequality states that the [[inner product]] of two vectors is always less or equal to the product of the norms of the two vector in any [[inner product space]].

== Mathematical statement ==

Let $V$ be an [[inner product space]] over $\mathbb{F}$.

$$\forall u,v\in V,\; |\langle u,v\rangle|\le\|u\|\|v\|.$$

Furthermore,

$$|\langle u,v\rangle|=\|u\|\|v\|\iff \exists \lambda\in\mathbb{F},\; u=\lambda v$$
<ref>{{#cite:Q1921}}</ref>

== Proof ==

If $v=0$, 

$$
|\langle u,v\rangle| = 0, \|u\|\|v\| = 0 \\
\therefore |\langle u,v\rangle| = \|u\|\|v\|
$$

If $v\neq 0$,

Consider the [[Orthogonality#Orthogonal_decomposition|orthogonal decomposition]]

$$u = \frac{\langle u, v \rangle}{\| v \|^2} v + u_2$$

where $u_2\bot v$. 

By the [[Orthogonality#Generalised_Pythagorean_theorem|generalised Pythagorean theorem]],

$$\| u \|^2 = \left\| \frac{\langle u, v \rangle}{\| v \|^2}v \right\|^2 + \| u_2 \|^2 
= \frac{|\langle u, v \rangle|^2}{\| v \|^2} + \| u_2 \|^2 $$

Since $v\neq 0$:

$$
\frac{|\langle u, v \rangle|^2}{\| v \|^2} + \| u_2 \|^2 \ge \frac{|\langle u, v \rangle|^2}{\| v \|^2} \\
\Rightarrow  \| u \|^2 \ge \frac{|\langle u, v \rangle|^2}{\| v \|^2} \\
\Rightarrow |\langle u,v\rangle|\le\|u\|\|v\|.
$$
